chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Asadi al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).

He said: Indeed God, blessed and exalted, is not described with time, nor with place, nor with motion, nor with transition, nor with stillness. Rather, He is the Creator of time, place, motion, stillness, and transition. He is far exalted above what the oppressors say, greatly exalted.

key_terms.الظَّالِمُونَ: Al-Zalimun (the oppressors/wrongdoers): Those who wrong God by attributing creaturely properties to Him
key_terms.خَالِقُ: Khaliq (Creator): God is the originator of all these categories, not subject to them
key_terms.يُوصَفُ: Yusaf (described): God cannot be characterized by created attributes

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about describing God with time, place, or motion?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq articulates a fundamental principle of Shia theology regarding divine transcendence (tanzih). The Imam categorically denies that God can be described by any physical or temporal attributes — time, place, motion, transition, or stillness — because these are all created things. Since God is their Creator, He cannot be subject to them. This teaching is directed against those who anthropomorphize God by attributing to Him spatial location, temporal existence, or physical movement.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Asadi al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa b. `Imran al-Nakha`I from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from `Ali b. Salim from Abi Basir from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as).

He said: Allah is not described with a time, nor with a place, nor with motion, nor with transition, nor with stillness. Rather, He is the Creator of time, place, motion, stillness, and transition. He is far above what the oppressors say.
